findings.text: THE method.md JUDGMENT (the crux) - omitting a docs/method.md section is a LEGITIMATE interpretation consistent with established release practice, NOT an incomplete W10. The W10 item text reads: 'make the docs true (the method and setup documents gain the architecture organ as shipped behavior, fully generic)'. A strict literal reading ('the method document AND the setup document') would name docs/method.md; the builder instead delivered the organ in docs/setup.md (7.8), docs/plugin.md (13), README, and docs/runbook.md (V.4), leaving docs/method.md unchanged, and flagged the call. I judge the builder's reading correct for five reasons, each verified: (1) ESTABLISHED PRACTICE - I inspected all three prior plan-release commits: WARP-0810 (PLAN-0008, b5e3e53) touched README + docs/plugin.md + packs/README.md, WARP-1008 (PLAN-0010, ab692f6) touched README + docs/plugin.md + docs/tracker-operator-guide.md, WARP-0908 (PLAN-0009, a791ddd) touched only README + version; NONE of the three touched docs/method.md. Even PLAN-0009's dedicated docs work item named 'the README, plugin guide, setup scaling, runbook, and the honesty manifest' - explicitly NOT method.md - while shipping a major capability (the fleet). This release actually documents MORE surfaces than any prior release (it adds setup.md 7.8 and plugin.md 13 and runbook V.4). (2) ROLE SPLIT - docs/method.md's own preamble is 'what WARP is and why it works' (the stable generic spine, v2.0), while docs/setup.md's preamble is 'The operational companion ... how you stand it up and keep it running'; a shipped capability/organ is operational and belongs in setup/plugin/runbook. (3) 'as SHIPPED BEHAVIOR' - documenting shipped behavior is definitionally the job of setup/plugin/runbook, not the timeless method spine, so 'the method and setup documents ... as shipped behavior' reads most coherently as the documents describing the method and its setup (the operational family), which the release did update. (4) method.md HISTORY - its only post-v2.0 content change (WARP-0909, a2423c7) added a genuine new METHOD PRINCIPLE (2.7.1 clean-context dispatch), not a capability release; PLAN-0011 is explicitly NOT a new principle (NG4 'No rebuild of the loop ... fills seams', Intent 'grows the missing organ from the method's own moves'). (5) RECEIPTS SCOPE - the plan's receipts language points the method-level exposition to the book chapter 'The Shape of the System' (the method's companion WRITING), which line 531 explicitly places OUT OF SCOPE for this repo. This is unlike the earlier dropped-surface findings that blocked prior W-items: those dropped MECHANICAL behavior the plan mandated; here the plan's established home for documenting a shipped capability is not method.md, and AC4 binds the unchanged-method.md decision transparently. I record this as a NOTE (not blocking): the wording is genuinely ambiguous and a stricter reading exists, so the human should be aware the builder made an interpretive call - but the call is well-founded and honestly disclosed, and every prior release settles the practice.

DOCS ARE HONEST WITH NO OVER-CLAIM (the second crux, Dmitry's HARD rule) - every doc addition is TRUE of what shipped, verified against ground truth rather than taken on faith. The blocking-vs-review split in README/plugin.md/setup.md matches the actual .warp/architecture.yaml enforcement labels one-for-one (module-size budget + engine invariants engine_byte_identical / derived_never_authoritative / adoption_safe_fail_closed are mechanizable and gate-blocking; dependency/import boundaries, function-length, duplication, complexity, and the stdlib/parser prose patterns are enforcement=review, review-lane), and the live gate emitted exactly those four review-lane notes plus 'mechanizable rules enforced; review-lane rules are reviewer guidance'. The docs state the contract is per-repo and never shipped (true: architecture.yaml is root-only), that the shape-fit and adversarial-decision reviewers are fail-loud reference seams with live prompt wiring per-repo and PENDING (true: LiveShapeReviewer and LiveAdversarialReviewer both RAISE rather than fabricate), that all monitoring is in-session with nothing detached (true: stdlib-only modules, verify.sh has zero entropy/restoration references), and that entropy/restoration are advisory and never gate-wired (true: absent from run_all, present only in a validate.py docstring). The docs consistently UNDER-claim (they foreground what is pending), the opposite of an over-claim. No honesty finding.

RELEASE SHAPE AND ADOPTION-SAFETY ARE CORRECT AND REPRODUCED. Two-commit shape: PLAN-0011 status ready->released lives IN the reviewed impl commit 0906fd1 (correct, because plans/ is outside the push guard's evidence-only allowlist), the version bump to 3.7.0 is in all three files, and WARP-1110's own spec stays draft in the impl commit (it flips to shipped in the evidence commit at landing, the reviewer's step). The impl commit touches no .warp/*.py and no protected path (verify.sh/warp-guard.sh/policy.yaml/policy_check.py untouched; the W2 shape hook was already shipped). The organ is byte-identical across all eight engine copies and adoption-safe: a freshly scaffolded repo runs GREEN with the shape gate standing down, carries the six validators but no contract, and excludes the two advisory derivations. release-check flips releasable exactly on WARP-1110's ship. All teeth (footprint load-bearing, pack-drift on divergence, release-check flip) reproduced.
